title: Never, nothing, no one
description: Say never, no longer, nothing, no one, only and neither…nor.
rule: Jamais (never), plus (no longer), rien (nothing) and personne (no one) replace pas: ne goes before the conjugated verb and the second word after it, and they are never combined with pas; after jamais and plus, un, une, des, du and de la become de, as after pas. Ne…que means only: que goes right before the thing restricted, becomes qu’ before a vowel, and the article stays (il ne boit que de l’eau). Ne…ni…ni means neither…nor: ni goes before each item, le, la and les stay, but un, une, des, du and de la disappear (elle n’a ni chien ni chat). In the passé composé, jamais, plus and rien go between the auxiliary and the participle (il n’a rien dit), but personne goes after the participle (il n’a vu personne). As subjects, rien and personne come first and ne still goes before the verb, with no pas (Personne ne répond). In a short answer with no verb, jamais, rien and personne stand alone, without ne.
example: Je ne fume plus. · Il n’a rien dit. · Personne ne répond.
aside: In speech ne is often dropped (je sais rien). Written French keeps it, and it matters with plus: je ne mange plus de pain means I no longer eat bread, while je mange plus de pain can mean I eat more bread.
